subject: Intermittent pool isolation — recovery plan, evidence package, and commercial options
messages:
From: Sara Thompson <sara@orbittech.com>
To: marcus.lin@redwood.ai
Cc: ops+orbit@orbittech.com
Date: 2027-11-10T08:32:00-07:00
Subject: Sudden token timeouts — dedicated pool responses dropping

Hi Marcus,

We're seeing intermittent 503/timeout errors against our dedicated pool starting ~07:45 PST. Throughput is fine most of the time but some requests stall for 8–15s and then fail. This spikes our client-side queuing and causes downstream alerts. Attached are a couple of request traces from our side.

Can Redwood confirm whether there's any ongoing maintenance or active autoscaler rollbacks in us-west? We're on reserved capacity (pool or-rt-34) and this is impacting a live campaign.

Thanks,
Sara Thompson
Head of Platform — OrbitTech
[Attachment: orbit-traces-07-45-07-58.json (3.2KB)]

From: marcus.lin@redwood.ai
To: Sara Thompson <sara@orbittech.com>, ops+orbit@orbittech.com
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, jordan.blake@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-11-10T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden token timeouts — dedicated pool responses dropping

Sara — thanks for the heads up and for the traces. Weve opened an incident (PL-8472) and our infra team is investigating. Initial check shows a brief network partition inside the us-west reserved cluster affecting a subset of GPUs and the autoscaler did not perform the expected fallback for those tenants.

Immediate next steps from our side:
- Full diagnostics collection (were bundling logs + kernel traces) and will send an evidence package within 3–4 hours.
- If degradation persists we will route your traffic to a hot fallback pool to restore latency within 15 minutes of your approval.
- We will prepare a post-incident timeline and a commercial proposal (service credit) for the impact window.

Apologies for the disruption — we understand this is high priority and we'll keep you updated every 2 hours until resolved.

— Marcus Lin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
To: Sara Thompson <sara@orbittech.com>, marcus.lin@redwood.ai
Cc: jordan.blake@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-11-10T11:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden token timeouts — dedicated pool responses dropping

Sara, Marcus — technical update from ops: 

What we observed: 
- At 07:44:22 PST a partial network isolation event affected nodes in the us-west-2 reserved cluster. The event caused a subset of GPU hosts to become briefly unreachable to the allocation plane.
- The allocator continued to schedule into healthy hosts but the autoscaler did not trigger fallback policies for tenants pinned to the impacted topology due to a race between the connectivity probe and the allocation controller.
- Result: some requests hit warm nodes and completed normally; others hit the isolated nodes and either queued in the local device layer (causing +8–15s latency) or returned a 503.

Immediate mitigations applied at 10:50 PST: 
- We moved OrbitTech traffic to the configured hot fallback pool (us-west-hot-2) per the routing playbook — this restored median latency to baseline within ~4 minutes.
- We performed a rolling reset of the affected NICs and applied an autoscaler controller patch to harden the probe ordering.

What we'll deliver by EOD: 
- Evidence package: host logs, allocator traces, and a summarized timeline (uploaded to the shared Drive link).
- A recommended action plan to prevent recurrence: stronger probe gating, conservative prewarming for pinned tenants, and a change to our fallback trigger thresholds.

Apologies again for the incident. We've also opened an internal RCA (RCA-PL-8472) and will share the postmortem with you within 3 business days.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Director, Reliability Engineering — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: diagnostics-20271110.zip (log bundle, 8.2MB)]

Subject: Commercial options following PL-8472 — proposed credit and runbook update

Sara — following the restored routing and Laura's timeline, I wanted to propose commercial remediation options so OrbitTech can plan next steps. Options were offering: 
1) Immediate service credit equal to 10% of November committed monthly spend applied to your next invoice;
2) Expanded monitoring & 90-day increased retention of per-request traces (no extra cost) so your team can run correlated analyses;
3) A one-time technical review call with the infra team to adjust prewarm and fallback thresholds (60-min session).

If you prefer, we can combine 1+2 or adjust the credit amount per the customer SLA conversation. Ive attached a short PDF with the formal credit wording for legal. Once you confirm which option you prefer I will route for sign-off and apply the credit.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Senior Customer Success Manager — Redwood Inference

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the transparency — the hot fallback routing brought our service back to acceptable levels. We reviewed the evidence package and confirmed the correlation between the NIC flaps and the request spikes. OrbitTech would like to accept option 1 + 2 (credit + extended trace retention). Please route the credit paperwork and schedule the technical review for next week (preferably 11/16 or 11/17 mornings PST).

One ask before the review: please include a short summary of the autoscaler controller patch and the proposed probe ordering change in the postmortem so our platform team can validate it against our fallback assumptions.

Appreciate the help — Sara
